questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks whether a court record of a tribute mission is fully reliable

options.text: Yes, because it lists goods
Yes, because it is official
No, because the court had an interest in framing the mission positively
No, because all records are worthless

questions.explanation: The court had an interest in positive framing, so the record is not fully reliable. But listing goods gives it some value.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Why a long voyage could sail at all
questions.learningObjective: Identify a resource a long voyage required

stimulus.body: A voyage account praises the captain's skill. It omits the supplies, crew size, and prior route knowledge that the court provided. The account was written to honor the captain.

questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks what this account omits

options.text: The existence of the voyage
The captain's name
The destination
Supplies, crew, and prior route knowledge

questions.explanation: The account omits supplies, crew, and route knowledge. It does not deny the captain, destination, or voyage.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a voyage record does not say
questions.learningObjective: Identify what a voyage record's silence implies
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks what a voyage record's silence about costs implies

options.text: Costs were definitely zero
Costs may have been high or politically sensitive
The record is complete
The voyage was free

questions.explanation: Silence about costs suggests they may have been high or sensitive. It does not prove zero cost or completeness.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: The cost of standardising a script
questions.learningObjective: Identify who bore the cost of script standardisation
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks who bore the cost of script standardisation

options.text: Only the emperor
No one, because change is free
Local scribes and readers who had to relearn forms
Foreigners who never wrote

questions.explanation: Local scribes and readers bore the cost of relearning. Change was not free, and foreigners were not the affected group.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: How a frontier was pushed outward
questions.learningObjective: Explain why frontier expansion often stalled
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks why frontier expansion often stalled

answer.exemplar: Supply lines stretched thin, local resistance persisted, and administration lagged, so expansion stalled until resources and governance caught up with claims.

questions.explanation: Supply stretched thin, resistance persisted, and administration lagged, so expansion stalled until governance caught up.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a claim of expansion rests on
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a claim that expansion was total

stimulus.body: A chronicle claims the realm expanded to its natural borders everywhere. It cites a few victories and tribute lists. It omits regions beyond effective control.

questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks how to read this total-expansion claim

options.text: As a weather report
As proven because victories occurred
As false because no expansion happened
As overstated because effective control was uneven

questions.explanation: The claim overstates by ignoring regions beyond effective control. Victories occurred but did not mean total control.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a tribute mission carried
questions.learningObjective: Identify what a tribute mission's goods imply
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks what a tribute mission's goods imply about the sending region

options.text: It had no products at all
It had products and people willing or able to travel
It was empty of people
It had no connection to the court

questions.explanation: Goods imply products and people able to travel. The other options deny the goods, staffing, or relationship.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Reading a court record of a tribute mission
questions.learningObjective: Identify a question a court record of a tribute mission cannot answer
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks which question a court record of a tribute mission cannot answer

options.text: When the mission occurred
What goods were exchanged
Whether the mission was truly voluntary
Who received the mission

questions.explanation: The court record cannot answer true voluntariness. Goods, date, and recipient are usually recorded.
questions.hint: What the court could not or would not record.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Why a long voyage could sail at all
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a claim that a voyage was effortless

stimulus.body: A court celebrates a voyage as effortless and triumphant. The celebration omits the planning, deaths, and costs. The celebration was held to honor the fleet.

questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks how to read this effortless claim

options.text: As a weather report
As proof that no effort was needed
As proof that no one died
As an interested account that omits effort and cost

questions.explanation: The celebration omits effort and cost, so effortless is not proven. Omission does not prove absence of deaths.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a voyage record does not say
questions.learningObjective: Identify what a voyage record's omissions protect
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks what a voyage record's omissions most likely protect

options.text: The sailors' privacy only
The reputation and interests of the funding court
Nothing, because records are complete
The destination's weather

questions.explanation: Omissions protect the funding court's reputation and interests. Records are not complete, and weather is not the motive.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: The cost of standardising a script
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a claim that standardisation erased all diversity

stimulus.body: A scholar claims standardisation erased all regional diversity in writing. The scholar notes that official documents became uniform but does not examine private letters or local records.

questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks how to read this erasure claim

options.text: As false because standardisation never happened
As proven because official documents were uniform
As overstated because private and local writing may have persisted
As a weather report

questions.explanation: The claim overstates by ignoring private and local writing. Official uniformity does not mean total erasure.
questions.hint: What the scholar did not examine.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: How a frontier was pushed outward
questions.learningObjective: Identify what frontier expansion required beyond military force
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks what frontier expansion required beyond military force

options.text: Nothing else at all
A single battle
A new name for the region
Settlement, administration, and supply lines

questions.explanation: Beyond force, expansion needed settlement, administration, and supply. A single battle, renaming, or nothing else is insufficient.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a claim of expansion rests on
questions.learningObjective: Explain why tribute alone does not prove expansion
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks why tribute alone does not prove expansion

answer.exemplar: Tribute can be sent by distant peoples who remain outside direct control, so it shows influence or submission, not administered territory.

questions.explanation: Tribute can come from peoples outside direct control, showing influence or submission, not administered territory.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a voyage record does not say
questions.learningObjective: Summarise what a voyage record's omissions mean for historians
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey asks what a voyage record's omissions mean for historians

answer.exemplar: Historians must read the record as a partial, interested account and seek other sources for costs, deaths, and dangers before judging the voyage's true price and success.

questions.explanation: Historians must treat the record as partial and interested, seeking other sources for costs, deaths, and dangers before judging success.
questions.hint: How to read a partial record.
